mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior 60 days reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25 percentage points over 60 days
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a similar 60-day pre-rate hike period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 50,000 jobs signals labor market strength that boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 50,000 by more than 10,000 jobs in a month
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive 5-day windows with PAYEMS > 50,000, SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (not directly observable but proxy via HOUST) exceed 600K units for two consecutive months, it indicates resilient consumer demand, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 600 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes where HOUST > 600 for >3 months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during the prior 60 days (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) below 101 for three consecutive months indicates softening supply constraints, lowering production costs and supporting higher equity valuations that drive positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window with INDPRO < 101 for >10 months, 60-day forward returns are not higher than average (median-based comparison).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of 0.3% or more for two months suggest accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady but signal future hikes, which depresses equity forward expectations and yields negative 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines by at least 0.6% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In inflation regimes with CPIAUCSL declines >0.5% for >4 months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% triggers a labor market tightening that increases wage growth expectations and corporate profits, producing positive 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 8 consecutive 5-day windows with UNRATE < 4%, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both the federal funds rate and the unemployment rate below historical averages (FEDFUNDS down, UNRATE down) create a dual signal of easing and strength that synergistically boosts equity valuations, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: dual easing and labor market strength
failure_condition: In regimes where both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE move in the same direction for >12 months, interaction effect is not statistically significant (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary policy easing regime (as indicated by FEDFUNDS trajectory), SPX 60-day forward returns tend to be higher than during a tightening regime, regardless of other macro variables.
candidate_trigger: regime: FEDFUNDS trajectory is consistently below a 2% moving average over the last 12 months
failure_condition: Over a 24-month period straddling two regimes, 60-day forward returns in the easing regime are not statistically higher than in the tightening regime (t-test p > 0.05).
